You... Watch movies at a faster speed? This is completely mind boggling to me. Why not just turn it off if you can't focus or find it too slow for you?

A podcast I can understand since it's usually pretty conversation heavy, but a movie or TV show is so bizzare.

Is this a normal thing people do??

I really enjoyed the film overall too and would probably rate it a 3.5-4 out of 5. I know what you mean about the pace levelling out. On the one hand, it risked a loss of tension and momentum, but on the other, I’d say that approach had its merits too. For me, it more accurately portrayed another level of horror that Iris was experiencing. I.e. the unrelenting, exhausting, protracted aspect of abduction. A lot of horror-thriller films are high octane, fight or flight throughout, but it could be said that this settled into a more realistic pace for the scenario. The fact that she was unable to fight or escape for most of it, reduced the action on screen, even limiting her facial expressions. However, I felt it also built tension, as I was waiting for the moment she’d explode back into action. The part where she falters (trying not to spoil for others, but hopefully you know the bit I mean), is a gut punch.

Despite her inability to move through most of it, they covered a surprising (physical) distance in inventive ways, which kept it visually interesting. 2 things that elevated this film for me were 1. The beautiful, open (and fantastically well shot) scenery, juxtaposed with her invisible corporal confinement. 2. The uncomfortable connection they forged by sharing details of their lives with one another. Both characters used that information against the other, creating a psychological “cat and mouse”. I felt they were mentally even-matched throughout, which helped to keep you guessing. Well acted too as you say.

I've been thinking about this for like 9 hours. I think OP had already gotten bored with the movie so wanted to speed up the slow burn parts maybe?

Hopefully.
I am a suspense thriller fan. But the movie was so predictable that you know what will happen next, I literally watched it in 1.5x
